### REQ-025: Fix min/max cycle energy model in the actuator PWM planner

## Requirement

The PWM cycle planner's goal is that the integral of valve opening over time equals the commanded duty cycle, modeling the thermal actuator as dead time + linear ramp. A simulation review on 2026-07-04 (`espidf/test/host/pwm_sim.cpp`, running the real `planCycle()` against a hold-during-dead-time/linear-ramp valve model) found the **normal PWM region (duty ≈ 0.17–0.83) exact to < 0.01%** — the ½-ramp accounting is provably correct — but three defects in the min/max special cycles (all present identically in the legacy firmware; not a migration regression):

1. **minCycle (duty < ≈0.133) delivers almost no heat (−57% … −100%).** The threshold `pMin = 2T·d / (½(OP+CL) + D0)` correctly prices a *full* open-close excursion (240 s area with default timing), but the pulse width `sw1 = sw2 − (pMin·OP − D1)` scales *linearly* while a partial excursion's area is *quadratic* in its peak. Worse, for duty < ≈0.089 the commanded on-time is shorter than the dead time D1 — the valve never physically moves. This creates an actuation dead zone: no duty in (0, ≈0.089) produces any heat, so low-demand rooms limit-cycle instead of trickle-heating.
2. **Stale switch times in the "second phase".** After a Min/Max cycle, `newCycle()` reverts to `CycleType::Normal` keeping the old sw1/sw2 while resetting the switch counter — the follow-up cycle re-fires one spurious switch at the stale sw1 (at low duty this spurious re-open is where the little delivered heat actually comes from). Intent per the legacy comment was "let the excursion tail play out"; that requires setting sw1 to the no-switch sentinel (3 × period) instead.
3. **maxCycle (duty > ≈0.867) over-delivers +5–9%.** Mirror of defect 1: the dip depth reaches only ~55% of the modeled `1 − pMax`; for duty ≥ ≈0.96 the off-pulse is shorter than D0 and no dip happens at all.

Fix direction: size the pulse by inverting the true area relation — required area A → peak `h` from `A = ½h²(OP+CL) + h·D0`, commanded on-time `= D1 + h·OP` (automatically ≥ dead time); mirror for the max-side dip; set second-phase switch times to the no-switch sentinel. Keep the `2T` amortization (excursion tail deliberately crossing the cycle boundary — that part of the design is sound).

## Notes

Full analysis in the 2026-07-04 session review; simulation harness and current error table documented in `espidf/test/host/README.md` and the `pwm_sim.cpp` header. Simulation assumes the valve holds position during dead times; if the thermal heads keep drifting during the dead window the numbers shift a few percent but all conclusions hold. Behavior is legacy-identical, so deployed devices have always had this characteristic (limit-cycling at low demand).

- **Implementation (2026-08-02):** all in `control/cycle_plan.h`, header-only, no
  interface change to `Actuator`.
  1. New `excursionHeight()` inverts `A(h) = ½h²(rampUp+rampDown) + h·deadReverse`
     so the pulse is sized by area instead of linearly. minCycle on-time is
     `D1 + h·OP` (structurally above the dead time → no dead zone); maxCycle
     off-time is the mirror `D0 + d·CL`.
  2. Second phase of a min/max cycle now sets both switch times to the
     no-switch sentinel instead of carrying stale values forward.
  3. **Beyond the three defects as written:** the min/max regions were keyed off
     `pMin`/`pMax` (duty < 0.133 / > 0.867), but the normal one-switch plan is
     only feasible for duty in [0.167, 0.833] — outside that its switch
     expression goes negative and clamps. The two gap bands were therefore
     silently distorted (+0.0134 at duty 0.14, −0.0134 at 0.86), which alone
     breaks the ≤ 0.01 criterion. The regions are now keyed off feasibility
     (`normalMinDuty`/`normalMaxDuty`), and an excursion whose demanded area
     exceeds a full excursion holds at the stop for the surplus. `pMin`/`pMax`
     are gone.

  Measured error (`pwm_sim`, default timing):

  | duty band | before | after |
  |-----------|--------|-------|
  | 0.01–0.04 | −100% (valve never moves) | ≤ 0.0001 abs |
  | 0.05–0.13 | −57% … −98% | ≤ 0.0001 abs |
  | 0.14–0.16 | +2.1% … +9.6% | ≤ 0.0001 abs |
  | 0.17–0.83 | exact | exact |
  | 0.84–0.86 | −0.4% … −1.6% | ≤ 0.0001 abs |
  | 0.87–0.95 | +5.2% … +8.8% | ≤ 0.0001 abs |
  | 0.96–0.99 | pinned fully open | ≤ 0.0001 abs |

  Note this changes the plan for duty 0.85-from-Closed and 0.15-from-Open, which
  REQ-017 pinned as regression checks: those duties now force the valve to the
  stop and plan the excursion from the opposite state next cycle, instead of
  clamping to an immediate switch. `cycle_plan_test` was updated accordingly;
  the REQ-017 no-wrap invariant remains covered by the full sweep.
